newsitem.title: USA: Owensboro says negotiates to buy S. American soy.
newsitem.headline: Owensboro says negotiates to buy S. American soy.

text.p: Owensboro Grain Co., a U.S. soybean crusher, is negotiating to buy more soybeans from South America, a company official said.
"We're definitely involved," the official said in response to market rumors about an impending deal.
The company official would not confirm tonnage, but other U.S. exporters said the deal involved up to two cargoes (100,000 tonnes) of soybeans.
In March, Owensboro purchased 150,000 tonnes of optional origin soybeans, and one of those cargoes was shipped from Brazil, Owensboro officials said earlier.
"There was a fixture yesterday for mid-May from Brazil to U.S. for soybeans," said one U.S. exporter. The exporter said the time-charter fixture was for a 50,000-tonne Panamax cargo of soybeans.
Shipping sources could not immediately confirm the fixture.
